name: Profhilo Structura

lead: Profhilo Structura is a hybrid hyaluronic acid product from IBSA, injected into superficial facial fat layers, mainly the lateral cheek. People use it for a fuller, lifted, better-supported midface.

It combines high- and low-molecular-weight hyaluronic acid into stable complexes using the NAHYCO process, without chemical cross-linking, and is described as addressing the loss of facial fat volume with age rather than acting as a conventional bolus filler. Authors propose it may influence fat tissue homeostasis, which is a hypothesis. Published data are a 22-person case series, an observational pilot study and lab comparisons, with a 164-person trial registered as ongoing.

paras: A clinician injects it with a cannula into each side of the face. Treatment is typically a short course of sessions, and results are described as developing over the following weeks.
Risks described for injectable hyaluronic acid include bruising, swelling and injection-site reactions. Product-specific safety data come from small studies, and it is given by trained clinicians.

chain: HA placed in superficial fat compartments
angle.text: People use Profhilo Structura to restore cheek volume and lift the midface. The hybrid hyaluronic acid is placed in superficial fat compartments to rebuild contour in the lateral cheek. Evidence so far is small case series.

lead: Profhilo Structura is an injectable hyaluronic acid (HA) product made by IBSA Farmaceutici, marketed as a medical device for restoring facial volume and contour, particularly in superficial fat compartments of the face such as the lateral cheek. It is a variant of the original Profhilo "skin remodelling" product and uses the same patented NAHYCO hybrid technology, which combines high- and low-molecular-weight HA into thermally stabilised complexes without chemical cross-linking.[1][2]

In a published case series, the product delivered 45 mg each of high-molecular-weight (about 1400 kDa) and low-molecular-weight (about 100 kDa) HA in a 2 mL syringe, and was placed with a cannula into the superficial fat compartment of each hemiface.[1] Its manufacturer-linked and independent clinicians describe it as a way to address the loss of facial fat volume associated with ageing, rather than as a conventional bolus filler.

Published evidence is limited to a small case series, an observational pilot study, laboratory comparisons with other HA fillers and a registered ongoing trial. These report improvements in clinician- and patient-rated measures, but they are small, uncontrolled and, in several cases, linked to the manufacturer.[1][2][3][4]

paras: Profhilo Structura is presented by its developers as a hybrid HA product with a much higher HA content than the original Profhilo. In the NAHYCO process, high- and low-molecular-weight HA chains are heated to form cooperative complexes; laboratory work comparing Profhilo, Profhilo Structura, a linear HA and cross-linked fillers examined how these products perform and how reversible they are with hyaluronidase.[1][2]

Unlike products designed mainly to add bulk, Profhilo Structura is described in the published literature as aiming to restore adipose tissue homeostasis, with HA proposed to influence adipocytes and surrounding tissue.[1] This mechanism is a hypothesis stated by the authors rather than an established finding.

The entry is discussed in the context of non-surgical face contouring, particularly "sunken" or flattened cheeks and mid-face support. Practitioners and patients describe it as a lower-bulk alternative to larger-volume fillers.[1][3] No community material on it is cited here.

A case series in the journal Gels followed 22 volunteers aged 36 to 60 years who received 2 mL of Profhilo Structura per hemiface via a 25-gauge cannula into the superficial fat compartment, and reported efficacy for adipose tissue restoration in the face.[1]

An observational pilot study published in 2024 examined the efficacy and tolerability of the product in the lateral cheek fat compartment.[3] A 2022 laboratory and in vivo comparison of four HA products, including Profhilo and Profhilo Structura, studied their performance and reversibility.[2]

A trial registered as NCT06719154 and titled as an evaluation of the safety and efficacy of Profhilo Structura began recruiting in September 2024 with a planned enrolment of 164 people with skin ageing.[4] Results were not available in the sources reviewed. No large independent randomised trials have been published.

As with other injectable HA products, procedures carry risks that clinicians describe, including bruising, swelling and injection-site reactions. Safety reporting specific to Profhilo Structura in the available sources is limited to small studies. Post-marketing surveillance of the broader Profhilo hybrid HA family has been published separately.[1][3]
